newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia pledges to privatize state enterprises.
newsitem.headline: Latvia pledges to privatize state enterprises.

text.p: Latvia's privatization agency said on Wednesday that it plans to distribute 750 million lats worth of privatization certificates in 1997 and 1998 to the public in a bid to spin off the country's largest state-run enterprises.

"We have taken a decision which will ensure public participation in the privatization process and we plan to issue certificates valued at up to 750 million lats," Viktor Shadinov, deputy director of the Latvian privatization agency, told a news conference.
He added that a number of large enterprises would be listed on the country's fledging bourse.
"Latvian Gas shares will be registered on the Riga Stock Exchange in 1997," he said, while the Latvian Shipping Company, with a capital base of $373 million, will be listed on the bourse in 1998.
Germany's Rurgas and Russia's Gazprom recently acquired a 15 percent stake each in Latvia Gas.

Latvia has made significant strides in its transition to a market economy since quitting the Soviet Union in 1991, and over half of its Gross Domestic Product is now attributable to the private sector.
